text:
max: heads up — found a pretty confusing DX bug in the Go generator streaming sample app during onboarding.
max: TL;DR: canceling the context mid-stream + token refresh on retry can lead to duplicate partial outputs in client apps.
lara: oof, can you paste a repro?
max: simplified repro below — using our sample app + default http auth refresher.
max: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, &gen.Request{Prompt: "long output..."})
for stream.Next() {
  fmt.Print(stream.Token()) // sometimes prints partial tokens twice after retry
}
```
max: behavior: when token rotates while stream is active, SDK does a retry under the hood, but the app sees a second set of partial tokens (looks like resumed + replayed chunk).
sam: is this reproducible with a short deadline only or with manual cancel too?
max: both. If I call cancel() after ~1s it sometimes triggers the refresh+retry path and duplicates.
jen: do we keep per-request sequence numbers server-side? should dedupe happen there?
lara: server does idempotency for non-stream requests, but streaming is different — we stitch segments. The runtime currently treats retry as a new stream attachment and doesn't tell the client that earlier tokens were already sent.
jen: hmm. sounds like two issues: (1) auth/refresh retries while streaming, (2) generator ergonomics — client surface doesn't make it easy to handle partial replays.
max: exactly. From a DX POV the sample app/docs are also confusing: the example shows passing ctx down but doesn't explain that token refresh can trigger internal retry. Newcomers assume cancel == final.
sam: any logs from the SDK side?
max: yes — attached snippet (abridged):
max: ```
[2026-07-14T12:00:01Z] gen: stream start req_id=abc
[2026-07-14T12:00:02Z] auth: token expired, refreshing
[2026-07-14T12:00:02Z] gen: retry attach req_id=abc-retry
[2026-07-14T12:00:03Z] client: ctx canceled
[2026-07-14T12:00:03Z] gen: sent chunk: "the quick"
[2026-07-14T12:00:03Z] gen: sent chunk: " brown fox" (replayed)
```
lara: thanks. That log makes the flow clear. We probably should: (A) avoid automatic retry for streaming when we detect client cancel, (B) make generator API surface return a typed error so apps can detect "stream canceled due to local ctx" vs "server-side retry/handoff".
sam: +1. Also recommend sample app update: show pattern with an explicit stream controller, e.g., StreamController{Ctx: ctx, OnRetry: func(...) { /* noop or dedupe */ }} so app authors can opt-in to dedupe.
jen: for short term patch: prevent auth-triggered retry while the original stream's ctx is Done. If auth refresh is required, surface an auth error instead of starting retry that will race with canceled ctx.
lara: agree. We should also add better docs around recommended backoff and how to wire up client's token provider so refresh happens before stream starts (proactive refresh).
max: I can prototype a small SDK change: add StreamOpts.RetryOnAuth bool (default false) so current behavior is opt-in. Then change docs/sample to call proactive token refresh in onboarding template.
jen: sounds reasonable. Also add a unit test that simulates token expiry mid-stream and expects either a clean error or no duplicate tokens.
sam: want me to pair on the test? I can do a randomized harness to catch replays.
max: yes please. I'll open a draft PR with the sample app change + docs and a minimal SDK flag.
lara: ping @ci-bot to run the integration harness when ready. :rocket:
ci-bot: started integration-run/streaming-auth-harness-17914 — status: queued
max: filed issue: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-1292 — includes logs and proposed API patch.
jen: awesome. Thanks for the detailed repro and suggested fixes — big DX win if we tighten this before more users hit it during onboarding. :+1:
max: will follow up with PR link later.
